title: #romeoandjuliet #romeoandjulietbroadway #romeoandjulietbway #kitconno...
transcript: Paul and I saw Romeo and Juliet shortly after it opened to mixed reviews and that verdict makes perfect sense to me. Headlined by Kit Connor and Rachel Zegler, this production is serviceable in that if you're going just for them, they deliver. They're both really good and they have amazing chemistry. And the other actors do a good job too, particularly Gabby Beans as Mercutio and The Friar. But beyond, that this production fell kind of flat for me. The vision seems to be very Gen Z vibes, and to me that's kind of all it was: just vibes. It wasn't particularly cohesive, and the tone was pretty inconsistent, like acts 1 and 2 felt like completely different plays, and the tragic parts weren't very tragic. Maybe that was intentional, but it didn't really seem like it. Also the staging was busy in a way that was kind of overstimulating and distracting. The directorial choices in general were pretty hit or miss for me. For example, I enjoyed a lot of the underscoring, and I enjoyed hearing Rachel sing toward the end of Act 1, but the song itself was super random. So yeah, I guess I was relying on the direction to make the show pop cause to me Romeo and Juliet relative to other Shakespeare plays is kind of mediocre. This production had an interesting concept but the execution didn't land. I enjoyed myself while I was watching it, as the performances were great and there were lots of exciting and creative usages of the space, but in retrospect it didn't live up to expectations — it was rather hollow. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The creator gives a balanced critique that neither recommends nor discourages attendance. While praising the lead performances and chemistry, they criticize the direction as inconsistent and hollow, concluding it 'didn't live up to expectations.'
